capabilities.title: PLS path modeling (classic, Mode A composites)
capabilities.description: Standard PLS-PM without consistency correction; reflective blocks are estimated as Mode A composites.

r-csem.implementation: `csem(.model with "=~", .disattenuate = FALSE)` — a plain "=~" call is PLSc because .disattenuate defaults to TRUE
r-csem.notes: Matches an independent reference implementation (_ref_pls.R) to 3e-16, seminr to 6e-15 and Python plspm to 5e-11 on tam-v1. Becomes supported when the Phase 3 adapter has reference tests.

r-seminr.notes: Not used for chunked bootstraps: seed S+1 replays seed S shifted by one draw.

py-plspm.implementation: c.Config(path, default_scale=Scale.NUM) with Mode.A blocks (or pre-standardised data with scaled=False)
py-plspm.notes: Agrees with cSEM to 5e-11 and with an independent reference (ref_pls.py) to 5e-10 on tam-v1. The default Config(scaled=True) 'metric' route divides every column by one pooled SD and is NOT standard PLS (paths off by 0.026, loadings by 0.22) — never use it. Unofficial GoogleCloudPlatform port; the repository has been archived (read-only) since 2026-07-30.

capabilities.title: Path inner weighting scheme
capabilities.description: Inner (structural) weighting scheme 'path' in the PLS iterative algorithm.

r-csem.notes: Schemes give different estimates (max |Δ| up to 0.009 on tam-v1), so the option is applied.

py-plspm.notes: Agrees with cSEM to ≤1.4e-10 on tam-v1.

capabilities.title: Centroid inner weighting scheme
capabilities.description: Inner (structural) weighting scheme 'centroid' in the PLS iterative algorithm.

r-csem.notes: Schemes give different estimates (max |Δ| up to 0.009 on tam-v1), so the option is applied.

py-plspm.notes: Agrees with cSEM to ≤1.4e-10 on tam-v1.

r-seminr.reason: seminr 2.6.0 offers path and factorial weighting only.

capabilities.title: Factorial inner weighting scheme
capabilities.description: Inner (structural) weighting scheme 'factorial' in the PLS iterative algorithm.

r-csem.notes: Schemes give different estimates (max |Δ| up to 0.009 on tam-v1), so the option is applied.

py-plspm.notes: Agrees with cSEM to ≤1.4e-10 on tam-v1.

capabilities.title: Composite / formative blocks (Mode B)
capabilities.description: Mode B outer weights (multiple regression of the inner proxy on the block's indicators).

r-csem.implementation: `"<~"` (defaults to Mode B); never "=~" with .PLS_modes = "modeB" and default .disattenuate

py-plspm.notes: Mixed and all-Mode-B models match ref_pls.py to 7.6e-10. A missing value in a Mode B block raises.

capabilities.title: Consistent PLS (PLSc)
capabilities.description: Consistency correction of Mode A composites so reflective constructs estimate common-factor parameters.

r-csem.notes: Matches _ref_pls.R and seminr (Δ 8e-15). Bootstrap keeps only ~90 of 100 draws on tam-v1 (inadmissible draws are counted and excluded).

py-plspm.reason: plspm has no consistent PLS. Use the R export (PLAN §2.9 parity policy).

capabilities.title: Cronbach's alpha, composite reliability (ρC) and AVE
capabilities.description: Internal consistency and convergent validity for reflective blocks; not applicable to composite/formative blocks.

capabilities.title: Dijkstra–Henseler ρA
capabilities.description: Consistent reliability coefficient for reflective blocks.

r-csem.implementation: `Estimates$Reliabilities` of a PLSc fit (weights are identical to the classic fit)
r-csem.notes: assess() on a classic (non-PLSc) object returns 1 for every block (defect, csem_assess.json); SEM Studio takes ρA from a PLSc run.

capabilities.title: HTMT and HTMT2
capabilities.description: Heterotrait–monotrait ratio of correlations (arithmetic and geometric-mean variants) for discriminant validity.

capabilities.title: Fornell–Larcker criterion
capabilities.description: Squared construct correlations compared with AVE.

capabilities.title: R², adjusted R², f² and VIF
capabilities.description: Explained variance, effect sizes and collinearity of structural predictors and Mode B indicators.

r-csem.notes: seminr's f² re-estimates the model without the predictor and differs from cSEM by 1.1e-3 on tam-v1; SEM Studio reports cSEM's definition and states it.

capabilities.title: SRMR, d_ULS and d_G
capabilities.description: Discrepancy measures between empirical and model-implied correlation matrices.

r-csem.notes: cSEM's d_G uses log10; the natural-log definition is about 5.3× larger. Shown with that definition stated; no CB-style cutoffs.

capabilities.title: Direct, total indirect and total effects
capabilities.description: Effect decomposition along structural paths.

r-csem.notes: total = direct + indirect holds exactly on tam-v1.

capabilities.title: Specific indirect effects
capabilities.description: Products of path coefficients along each mediation route, with bootstrap intervals.

r-csem.reason: cSEM does not report specific indirect effects; SEM Studio's adapter computes the products from each bootstrap draw (Phase 3).

capabilities.title: Bootstrap with percentile intervals
capabilities.description: Case resampling with a mandatory seed; percentile confidence intervals from the raw draws.

r-csem.implementation: `resamplecSEMResults(.resample_method = "bootstrap", .R, .seed)`; intervals = quantile(type = 7) of the concatenated chunk draws
r-csem.notes: Draws depend only on (seed, i) and are identical across future plans; our quantile(type 7) equals infer()$CI_percentile exactly. Always pass .seed (NULL is not reproducible even after set.seed). One erroring replication aborts the whole call.

r-lavaan.notes: lavaan's 'perc' interval is boot's norm.inter interpolation, not quantile(); its SE uses divisor R.

r-seminr.reason: Consecutive seeds replay the same draws shifted by one, which breaks chunked bootstrapping.

py-plspm.reason: plspm's bootstrap has no seed argument: under spawn (macOS) the seed is ignored, under fork with processes>1 every child draws the same resamples, and failed resamples are dropped silently. Python exports use an app-owned seeded loop that counts failures instead.

py-semopy.reason: semopy has no nonparametric bootstrap (only a parametric bias correction).

capabilities.title: Bootstrap BCa intervals
capabilities.description: Bias-corrected and accelerated intervals.

r-csem.reason: CI_bca ran but its numbers are not yet checked; it re-runs an n-row jackknife on every infer() call.

r-lavaan.reason: bca.simple ran but is unchecked; full bca fails when R < N.

capabilities.title: Replace inadmissible bootstrap draws
capabilities.description: Redraw until admissible instead of excluding.

r-csem.reason: Replacements are drawn with seed+1 (cSEM source), which collides with the next chunk's seed. SEM Studio excludes and counts inadmissible draws.

capabilities.title: Individual sign-change correction
capabilities.description: Per-parameter sign alignment of bootstrap draws.

r-csem.reason: `.sign_change_option = "individual"` silently drops draws (55 rows kept while the count says 100). Not offered.

capabilities.title: Construct-level IPMA
capabilities.description: Importance = unstandardized total effect on a chosen target; performance = 0–100 score from the ORIGINAL scale endpoints.

r-csem.implementation: computed by SEM Studio from a classic PLS fit on endpoint-rescaled data
r-csem.notes: doIPMA() never rescales; it matches the first-principles computation to 9e-14 only when the data were rescaled to 0–100 beforehand. Must not run on a PLSc fit. Implementation in Phase 4.

capabilities.title: Indicator-level IPMA
capabilities.description: Importance and performance of individual indicators.

r-csem.reason: Ran on tam-v1 without error; numbers not yet checked.

r-csem.reason: Ran on tam-v1 without error; numbers not yet checked.

r-csem.reason: Ran on tam-v1 without error; numbers not yet checked.

capabilities.title: Endogeneity tests (Hausman / Gaussian copula)

r-csem.reason: testHausman requires instruments, which the model contract cannot express yet.

capabilities.title: Maximum likelihood CFA / SEM
capabilities.description: Common-factor model estimated by normal-theory ML.

r-lavaan.notes: Checked by identities: χ² = N·F_ML, CFI/TLI/RMSEA/SRMR/AIC/BIC from their definitions, delta-method SEs, ML regression = OLS on a saturated case. Not yet compared with an independent ML implementation.

py-semopy.notes: Σ and F_ML rebuilt by hand to 8e-15; covariance divisor N; chi2 = N·F_ML; SEs from expected information. inspect() returns '-' for fixed parameters (object columns).

capabilities.title: Robust ML (MLR)
capabilities.description: ML estimates with robust standard errors and scaled test statistic.

py-semopy.reason: semopy offers se_robust=True (sandwich SEs, changed SEs by up to 3×) but no scaled test statistic; not equivalent to lavaan's MLR/MLM. Unchecked.

capabilities.title: Robust ML (MLM)
capabilities.description: ML estimates with robust standard errors and scaled test statistic.

py-semopy.reason: semopy offers se_robust=True (sandwich SEs, changed SEs by up to 3×) but no scaled test statistic; not equivalent to lavaan's MLR/MLM. Unchecked.

capabilities.title: Ordinal indicators (WLSMV / DWLS)
capabilities.description: Polychoric-based estimation for ordered categorical indicators.

r-lavaan.reason: Ran on tam-v1; numbers not yet checked against the ordinal synthetic fixture.

capabilities.title: Full-information ML for missing data
capabilities.description: Uses all available data under MAR.

r-lavaan.reason: Ran with ML and MLR (MLM and WLSMV are rejected by lavaan); numbers to be checked on the missing-mcar fixture.

py-semopy.reason: Use ModelMeans(obj="ML"); NEVER Model(obj="FIML"), which has no mean structure and silently assumes zero means (parameters off by up to 43 on raw data). ModelMeans(obj="FIML") raises NotImplementedError. A Model fit on data with NaN silently uses pairwise covariances.

capabilities.title: Global fit indices
capabilities.description: χ², df, p, CFI, TLI, RMSEA with CI, SRMR, AIC, BIC and scaled variants.

r-lavaan.implementation: `fitMeasures()` (errors if the model did not converge — check first)

py-semopy.notes: Verified: chi2, DoF, CFI, TLI, NFI, RMSEA (≤5e-9). NOT reported by SEM Studio: GFI (it equals NFI), AGFI, LogLik/AIC/BIC (LogLik is the F_ML value). SRMR and the RMSEA CI are absent. chi2 p-values underflow to 0.0.

capabilities.title: Estimation diagnostics
capabilities.description: Non-convergence, Heywood cases, non-positive-definite matrices and non-identification surfaced as warnings.

r-lavaan.implementation: `lavInspect(fit, "converged")`, `lavInspect(fit, "post.check")`, negative variances; problems arrive as warnings with a fit object still returned

py-semopy.reason: semopy bounds variances at 0: a Heywood case that needs θ = −0.62 returns 3e-11 with success=True, an ordinary SE and no flag. Python exports must check boundary estimates themselves and say so.

capabilities.title: Modification indices
capabilities.description: Diagnostic suggestions only; never applied automatically.
